question: Why was probenecid, a drug now taken for gout, first developed around 1950?
answer: To make scarce penicillin last longer. The kidneys pump penicillin actively into the urine, clearing it within hours. Karl Beyer's team at Sharp & Dohme designed a molecule that competes for the same pump, so penicillin stays in the blood longer and at higher levels. It also stops the kidneys reclaiming uric acid, hence gout.
move: When supply is short, slow the leak before building more.
source: Beyer et al., American Journal of Physiology, 1951
reference: Beyer, Russo, Tillson, Miller, Verwey & Gass, 'Benemid', p-(di-n-propylsulfamyl)-benzoic acid: its renal affinity and its elimination, American Journal of Physiology, 1951
